issue.title: tests/completion/test_snapshot.py drift nodes flake under check-full's full parallel lane
issue.description:
Discovered while landing an unrelated agent-role phase-label rename (docs/ace.md + prompt_panel widgets) via just check-full in workspace sase_13.

REPRODUCTION: tests/completion/test_snapshot.py::test_checked_in_snapshot_has_no_drift and ::test_current_structural_view_matches_checked_in_snapshot both pass in isolation on current HEAD (.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:randomly -q tests/completion/test_snapshot.py -- 2 passed), and 'just sync-completion-spec' (tools/sync_completion_spec --write) produces no diff against the checked-in cli_spec.json. selection-health's durable record store (/home/bryan/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase/) holds two recent full-run failure records for both nodes -- 20260818T114432Z-134839e82d2e-650306-full-run.json (recorded_at 2026-08-18T11:50:27Z) and 20260818T120830Z-134839e82d2e-1244116-full-run.json (recorded_at 2026-08-18T12:14:36Z) -- both stamped head=134839e82d2e (a commit that already contains the epic-symbols fix from 1482fc1dc, verified an ancestor via git merge-base --is-ancestor) but tree_dirty=true, i.e. the recording workspace had uncommitted local changes to CLI/argparse surface at the time.

ROOT CAUSE: cli_spec.json is a checked-in structural snapshot of the argparse tree (tests/completion/test_snapshot.py); any workspace with uncommitted CLI-surface changes, or any commit that adds argparse surface without also running 'just sync-completion-spec' in the same commit, makes the node fail there without that being a defect in the node itself. Epic sase-oc (closed) hit and understood the same underlying mechanism for a different drift instance (the .root.subcommands[bead].subcommands[epic-symbols] node from fa1948437 vs phase sase-oc.1's stale snapshot); this is the same class recurring, not a new bug. Phase bead sase-p3.14 independently flagged the same two nodes (plus 3 others already tracked elsewhere) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-18T08:09:50Z, corroborating this is cross-workspace noise, not something caused by this workspace's change.

IMPACT: blocks 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' (the last gate of 'just check-full') for every unrelated change landing while the durable store still holds these dirty-tree records, even though the checked-in snapshot is not actually stale on any clean tree tested.

task_type_fields.evidence: Fails only in full-run records with tree_dirty=true (uncommitted local CLI changes in the recording workspace); passes in isolation and against the checked-in snapshot on every clean tree tested, including current HEAD. The sibling node test_current_structural_view_matches_checked_in_snapshot fails/passes identically in the same records -- same root cause, tracked together here rather than as a second bead.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-oc — closed epic that hit and understood the same cli_spec.json drift mechanism for a different instance (the epic-symbols node from fa1948437 vs phase sase-oc.1's stale snapshot).
RELATED: sase-p3.14 — independently flagged the same two nodes as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-18T08:09:50Z; epic sase-p3 has not yet landed to triage that note into a task bead.

evidence.note: Independently reproduced while implementing tribe_panel_settled_monitor_gear.md (unrelated tree, no CLI/argparse changes in this diff). Discrepancy worth flagging: this bead's diagnosis says the two nodes pass in isolation on a clean HEAD and 'just sync-completion-spec' produces no diff -- but on my workspace's clean master HEAD (4cf7672bd, git stash of my unrelated changes), tools/sync_completion_spec reports real drift every time (not just in full-parallel-lane dirty-tree records), and both nodes fail in isolation too: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/completion/test_snapshot.py::test_checked_in_snapshot_has_no_drift tests/completion/test_snapshot.py::test_current_structural_view_matches_checked_in_snapshot -q -> 2 failed, reproduced twice. My origin/master is 4 commits ahead of my local HEAD, so this may be a real regression that landed after this bead's original 09:43 EDT report rather than the described dirty-tree flake. Worth re-checking whether the checked-in cli_spec.json still matches current argparse surface before assuming this is cross-workspace noise.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-qx.2 / sase-qx.4 / sase-qx.5 — three sase-qx phases proposed the same two tests/completion/test_snapshot.py nodes as follow-up (cli_spec.json drift / monitor-start description_digest). Routed here rather than a new task. On this land-agent tree, both nodes passed in isolation (2 passed in 7.88s via pytest -p no:randomly). Did not reproduce live drift, so no +1.

evidence.note: PROPOSED BY sase-r0.1 and sase-r0.2 while landing tmux Agent. Both phases saw tests/completion/test_snapshot.py::test_checked_in_snapshot_has_no_drift and ::test_current_structural_view_matches_checked_in_snapshot fail after just check escalated (Justfile/schema/default_config.yml). r0.1: fails on this tree even with no local CLI changes and also fails on a clean tree. r0.2: argparse-tree vs snapshot key-order drift, not caused by llm_interactive_cli. Independent of the original dirty-tree diagnosis; matches the later isolation-fail evidence already on this bead.
